page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-22-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, offering 22 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 11 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 88 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware instruction extensions, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, backed by 105 MB of shared L3 cache.

Storage is a core component of this instance profile, which includes 1608 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage distributed across four local drives. It does not provision discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on CPU and I/O execution. Benchmark tests place overall compute performance squarely in the mid-range of its peer group, scoring 1,724 in Geekbench single-core and 12,136 in multi-core metrics. Memory subsystems demonstrate 109.64 GB/sec read and 47.22 GB/sec write throughput on large un-cached blocks, while Redis SET operations sustain 24.06 million operations per second. Text generation on smaller language models (135M) reaches a strong 293.95 tokens per second, benefiting directly from onboard AMX acceleration.

Cost efficiency is driven by the co-location of high-density local NVMe storage with balanced general-purpose compute, removing the need for separate block storage attachment costs for IOPS-intensive tasks. Because local SSDs are ephemeral, operational tradeoffs require architectural resilience against instance termination or redeployment. This hardware profile is best aligned with transactional databases, caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and continuous integration pipelines that demand low-latency scratch disk I/O alongside steady CPU execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-22-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 22 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz and 88 GB of memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, it features 1608 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage across four physical disks, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the middle performance tier for standard compute, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,136 and handling 24.06 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput sustains 109.64 GB/sec read speeds on large un-cached blocks, while AMX support drives fast text generation on compact language models. The integration of high-speed local storage directly into a balanced compute configuration provides solid qualitative resource efficiency for scratch space and fast read-write cycles, making it suitable for relational databases, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD runners, and data preprocessing pipelines.
